_comment: Taxpayer profile — filled by /tax-setup interview. Used by all skills to determine applicable forms.
_security: NEVER store full SSNs. Use last 4 digits only. If version-controlled, add taxpayer_profile.json to .gitignore before first commit.
_validation: All fields must be sanitized: state must be a 2-letter US state code (e.g. CA, NY); ssn_last4 must be exactly 4 digits; names must contain only letters, hyphens, apostrophes, and spaces; zip must be 5 or 9 digits. Reject values containing shell metacharacters ($, `, !, ;, |, &) or control characters.

residency._comment: ASSERTED residency, which address.state is not: that is a mailing address, and a taxpayer can be a full-year resident of TWO states at once. domicile_state is the one place intended as the permanent home (there is exactly one, and it need not equal address.state). days_present_by_state and abode_months_by_state are per-state COUNTS for the tax year, keyed by 2-letter code, and they are counts rather than flags on purpose: a statutory test with a discontinuity has no honest boolean answer near the line. A month counts when a home was maintained there and available year-round, owned or not. telecommutes_for_out_of_state_employer changes the NONRESIDENT allocation, not the residency test — a remote day can still be a work day in the employer's state. Absent or empty means the questions were not asked, which is NOT the same as a negative answer; flags.statutory_resident_of_another_state carries the taxpayer's own conclusion and is what the capability gate reads. docs/contributing/residency-guardrails.md

flags._comment_foreign_funds: Foreign-fund/PFIC + sanctioned-holding gate (see foreign_holdings_detail). has_pfic_taxable_event = a NON-US-domiciled fund/ETF had a distribution OR was sold this year → BLOCKS by default (the §1291 regime is punitive and the normal qualified-dividend/LTCG path would understate). This is NOT a permanent hand-off: /tax-compute DOES compute the §1291 excess-distribution/disposition tax (compute_pfic_excess_distribution + compute_pfic_1291) from the foreign_holdings_detail facts once the block is ACKNOWLEDGED — collect the required facts (acquisition/event dates, distributions_by_year, disposition_gain_usd, pfic_election, fund_domicile, preceding_holding_years) and run it. Only pfic_election==none funds are computed; QEF/§1296-MTM funds and a complete=False result (missing historical rate / uncovered §6621 quarter / short distribution history) stay hand-prepared and keep the return INCOMPLETE. If has_foreign_mutual_funds is true this MUST be answered explicitly (absent → capability gate blocks, not a silent 'no'). has_foreign_financial_account = holdings at a foreign (non-US) broker/custodian → Form 8938 reporting surface (complements FBAR). has_sanctioned_blocked_asset = an OFAC-blocked/frozen holding → blocked-income + §165(g) worthlessness are hand-analyzed (do NOT auto-claim a loss). has_foreign_bond = directly-held foreign-currency bond → §1272 OID accrues + coupon interest translates to Schedule B EVERY year held (MANUAL), and a disposition splits via compute_section_988. All read False when absent (legacy profiles pass); the broader has_foreign_mutual_funds MANUAL note remains the net.
flags._comment_fl_business_tangible_property: SITUS flag, not a residence flag, AND a filing-obligation flag, not a mere ownership flag: true iff a DR-405 filing is ACTUALLY EXPECTED THIS year for tangible personal property used in any BUSINESS OR RENTAL activity PHYSICALLY LOCATED in Florida on January 1 (F.S. 193.062, DR-405) — independent of where the taxpayer lives. DR-405 is filed PER COUNTY/PER ACCOUNT with that county's property appraiser (floridarevenue.com TPP guidance), so a taxpayer with property in multiple FL counties has a SEPARATE filing history, $25,000 test, and waiver status for EACH one — this flag is true iff ANY ONE county/account requires a filing THIS year: its INITIAL DR-405 has NOT yet been filed, OR its property's value AS OF JANUARY 1 of the tax year (not its value at interview time) exceeds $25,000, OR its county property appraiser has requested a return this year. Only when EVERY county/account clears the F.S. 196.183 continuing-filer waiver (initial already filed, value at or below $25,000, no appraiser request, for ALL of them) — leave this flag false and record a note in answers.md instead (re-ask next year for every county, since value/appraiser requests can change independently per county). Covers a landlord's rental-unit furnishings/appliances/equipment, not just a sole proprietorship's business equipment. A non-FL-resident with FL business/rental equipment still owes the county filing when a filing is expected; a FL resident whose property sits in another state does not need FL's DR-405 for that property (record the other state as a limitations note, not an event).
flags._comment_obbba_sch1a: has_qualified_tips / has_qualified_overtime / has_car_loan_interest drive the OBBBA Schedule 1-A BELOW-AGI deductions (line 13b, TY2025-2028). Overtime is the FLSA premium portion only. These are computed, not gated.
flags._comment_filed_extension: Set by /tax-extend (not the interview). Drives the Apr-15 pay-by + Oct-15 extended-deadline events in tax_calendar_{year}.ics.
flags._comment_nyc_resident_spouses: How many spouses were New York City residents for the WHOLE year: 0, 1 or 2. Only meaningful on a joint return, and REQUIRED there — IT-201 line 47 is not used at all when exactly one spouse was a city resident (that return goes to line 51, a computation this engine does not do). One household boolean cannot carry it: nyc_resident says whether the household owes city tax, and this says whether BOTH spouses are residents. Assuming two over-states the city tax for a mixed-residence couple by the non-resident spouse's whole share.
flags._comment_statutory_residency: Set when the taxpayer meets ANOTHER state's mechanical residency test while resident here — it can apply whatever their domicile is, and two resident states tax the same income with a credit this toolkit does not model, so it BLOCKS. DISTINCT from moved_states_this_year (a mid-year MOVE) and has_nonresident_source_income (income SOURCED elsewhere). For New York the capability gate derives it from residency.days_present_by_state and residency.abode_months_by_state rather than trusting this flag alone. The thresholds, their sources and the dates they were read: docs/contributing/residency-guardrails.md
flags._comment_age_65: 65-or-older by year end. Drives the §63(f) additional standard deduction AND the separate OBBBA §70103 enhanced senior deduction (Schedule 1-A line 13b — they stack). Spouse flag counts only on a JOINT return.

_comment_acknowledged_limitations: Rule ids from agents/lib/capabilities.py the taxpayer has EXPLICITLY accepted proceeding without (decision recorded in answers.md). An id here downgrades that blocking gap to a limitations-manifest entry. Unknown ids hard-error so a typo cannot silently unblock nothing.

hsa_detail._comment: Form 8889 return-side HSA test (N3a). eligible_months = # months you were an HSA-eligible individual (HDHP coverage on the 1st, no disqualifying coverage). coverage_type = self_only | family | none. last_month_rule = eligible on Dec 1 (full annual limit, but a testing period applies). REQUIRED for the return-side excess check when has_hsa — without eligible_months the case stays MANUAL (a full-year assumption would MISS a partial-year excess + its 6% excise). family_limit_share: for married-both-HDHP, this spouse's fraction of the family limit.

dependent_care_detail._comment: Form 2441 §21 credit (N3b) eligibility facts + inputs, collected by /tax-setup when has_dependent_care. GATES (attested): qualifying_persons = count of qualifying persons (under 13, OR incapable of self-care meeting relationship/residency). work_related_confirmed = both spouses (if married) worked / looked for work / were full-time students. provider_tin_on_file = provider name + TIN collected (due diligence). INPUTS: qualified_expenses paid; employer_dcb = W-2 box 10 excluded benefits; taxpayer/spouse student_disabled_months for §21(d)(2) deemed income; mfs_lived_apart_exception for the §21(e)(2) MFS carve-out. Earned income comes from the computed return.

foreign_holdings_detail._comment: Structured foreign-holding facts feeding the capability gate + the §988 bond computation (P3) + the §1291 PFIC engine (P4). One entry per holding in `holdings`. kind = fund | bond | other_security (fund vs debt is load-bearing: a fund can be a PFIC, a bond cannot). fund_domicile = 2-letter country of the FUND's registration (PFIC test is domicile, NOT holdings — a US fund of foreign stocks is NOT a PFIC). custody = foreign_broker | us_broker | direct_registered (drives Form 8938 / FBAR — a US-broker account is generally excluded). currency = ISO-4217 (non-USD debt → §988 ordinary FX gain/loss). blocked_by_sanctions + blocking_event_date = OFAC path. pfic_election = none | qef | mtm (+ election_first_year) — a timely election changes the §1291 default (ONLY `none` funds are computed; qef/mtm stay blocked). received_distribution / disposed = the §1291 taxable-event triggers (drive has_pfic_taxable_event) and the §1298(f) reporting test with aggregate_pfic_value. The gate reads the derived flags; compute_section_988 reads the bond entries (currency, fc_cost/fc_proceeds, acquisition/disposition spot rates). **§1291 compute inputs (P4), per PFIC fund with a taxable event:** fund_id (a STABLE, DISTINCT per-fund identifier — ISIN/CUSIP or a slug — that the Step 12.7 tie-out matches against the computed form_8621_pfic.funds[] entry; a taxable no-election fund with no matching complete result FAILS the gate, so every taxable fund needs a UNIQUE one); acquisition_date (ISO; the holding period runs the day AFTER acquisition through the event, §1223); **the event DATE(S) — a distribution and a disposition in the SAME year are SEPARATE §1291 events with DIFFERENT allocation endpoints, so carry BOTH `distribution_date` and `disposition_date` (ISO) when both occur** (event_date is the single-event convenience alias = whichever one applies; each §1291 computation uses its own date); preceding_holding_years (# tax years held before the current year — REQUIRED for a non-first-year distribution or the excess-distribution result is INCOMPLETE); distributions_by_year ({year: USD total} — the FULL zero-inclusive base-period history, summed per fund per year, for the §1291(b) 125% test); disposition_gain_usd (the SIGNED proceeds − basis for EVERY sale, INCLUDING a negative loss — only a POSITIVE gain is routed through §1291, a loss is a Schedule D capital loss, but the signed amount MUST be recorded because the tie-out treats a `disposed` holding with no finite value as an unverifiable event and BLOCKS the return); position_fully_closed (bool — true iff the disposition CLOSED the whole position; a PARTIAL sale is false so /tax-rollover retains the remaining shares + history). v1 computes PFIC-FROM-ACQUISITION only; a fund that became a PFIC AFTER acquisition (mid-holding transition) is BLOCKED (compute_pfic_1291 raises — hand-prepare Form 8621). History carried year-over-year by /tax-rollover.

prior_year._comment_capital_loss_carryforward: The SPLIT fields feed Schedule D line 6 (short-term) and line 14 (long-term); /tax-rollover fills them from the prior result.json schedule_d.loss_carryforward_to_next_year block. `capital_loss_carryforward` is the LEGACY combined figure: when it is non-zero and both split fields are zero, /tax-compute STOPS and asks for the split from the prior return's Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet (lines 8 and 13) — a combined figure is never split by guess.
prior_year._comment_amt_credit: Form 8801 minimum tax credit from prior-year deferral-item AMT (ISO exercises). Rolled forward by /tax-rollover from prior result.json form_6251.form_8801_carryforward_to_next_year; consumed via compute_form_8801_credit (Schedule 3 line 6b).
prior_year._comment_ca_amt_credit: CA Schedule P (540) AMT credit from prior-year deferral-item CA AMT (ISO exercises). A SEPARATE carryforward from the federal one (CA exemption/TMT differ). Rolled forward by /tax-rollover from prior result.json california_540.schedule_p.carryforward_to_next_year.
prior_year._comment_ira_basis: Form 8606 line 14 nondeductible traditional-IRA basis carried from the prior year. Rolled forward by /tax-rollover from prior result.json form_8606.basis_remaining.

expected_sources._comment: Payers/institutions seen in prior year. Informs /tax-parse to flag missing documents. EINs are public business identifiers — full values stored (not last-4-only like individual SSNs).
